texts.preamble: Birendra Kumar Barnwal vs The State Of Jharkhand ......... Opp. ... on 31 July, 2018 Author: Anant Bijay Singh Bench: Anant Bijay Singh In The High Court Of Jharkhand At Ranchi Cr. Rev. No. 339 of 2001 Birendra Kumar Barnwal ...... Petitioner(s) Versus The State of Jharkhand ......... Opp. Party(s) ------
texts.facts: The Food Inspector served notice upon the petitioner demanding sample of Haldi powder and mustered oil for sending the same to the Public analyst. 125 X 3 grams of mustered oil and 100 x 3 grams of Haldi powder was purchased by the Food Inspector and by observing all the legal paraphernalia, he sealed three files of mustered oil along with three packets of Haldi powder amounting to 100 grams each and sent the same by registered parcel along with the specimens of Birendra Kumar Barnwal vs The State Of Jharkhand ......... Opp. ... on 31 July, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129471472/ 1 seal and memorandum. It is further alleged that memorandum and specimen of seal were sent separately to the Public Analyst, Patna, who in course of test found Haldi powder to be adulterated because of the fact that it did not confirm to the prescribed standard and submitted his report accordingly. The food inspector received the report of the public analyst, Patna and prepared a prosecution report, solicited the sanction from the competent authority and filed the same in the court of the then A.C.J.M., Koderma. The further case of the prosecution is that one copy of the analyst report was also sent to the petitioner. This Cr. Revision application was filed on 23.08.2001 and the case was admitted on 17.10.2001 and bail was granted to the petitioner. Thereafter, on 28.02.2017, L.C.R was called for . that the public analysis report is to be sent to the petitioner, so that he may raise objection and also may apply to the competent court to send the sample for Public Analyst test. In the instant case, no notice was given to he petitioner, nor copy of the Public Analysis report was also sent to the petitioner. In para- 8 of the judgment, it has been stated that a copy of the memorandum and seal was separately sent to the Public Analyst vide registered parcel and the rest 2 files of Haldi Powder and mustered oil were sent in the office of the A.C.M.O., Hazaribagh for which a receipt Ext.7 has been produced and marked. It has further come on evidence that report of the public analyst showing the powder Haldi was received which has been marked Ext.8. Subsequently, the prosecutions report was filed and accordingly, the prosecution report has been marked Ext.9.
texts.arguments: The learned counsel for the petitioner, while assailing the impugned Judgment referred to Section 13(2) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 which reads as under :- "13. Report of Public Analyst(1).................... (2) On receipt of the report of the result of the analysis under sub-section(1) to the effect that the article of food is adulterated, the Local(Health) Authority shall, after the institution of prosecution against the persons from whom the sample of the article of food was taken and the person, if any, whose name address and other particulars have been disclosed under 14-A forward, in such manner as may be prescribed, a copy of the report of the result of the analysis to such person or persons, as the case may be, informing such person or persons that if it is so desired, either or both of them may make an application to the court within a period of ten days from the date of receipt of the copy of the report to get the sample of the article of food kept by the local (Health) Authority analysed by the Central Food Laboratory". In view of Section 13(2) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954, the mandatory requirement is
